live.what_this_is: The record of the tag-gated live run against real Google. scripts/emit-evidence.sh cannot execute these tests — they need a real OAuth client, a human at a consent screen, a running homeplane-server and a running ToolHive workload — so it embeds this file verbatim under the artifact's "live" key. Nothing in the tooling can vouch for what is written here; it carries its own commit, timestamps and caveats so a reader can judge it.
live.recorded_by: the worker that ran the proof, transcribed from the run's captured stdout
live.commit_note: The green run finished at 2026-08-13T23:09:44Z and the tree it ran on was committed as this SHA 3m07s later. The running worker did not capture a tree hash at invocation time, so this SHA is the closest verifiable anchor, NOT a checksum of the bytes that ran.
caveats: The Calendar legs (six-op) were run BEFORE the send_updates capability guard was added to the manifest, so their manage_event calls carried no send_updates argument. Under the current manifest those exact calls are REFUSED (connector.send missing) and a legitimate caller must pass send_updates:"none". The proof of what Google does end to end still stands; the proof that the CURRENT argument shape works against Google does not. Re-run the Calendar legs and replace this file before treating it as attesting to the guarded manifest.
The Drive read, Drive write-refusal, consent/custody and revocation legs are unaffected by the guard — none of them calls manage_event.
The gateway ran on loopback with the ToolHive workload's egress unrestricted; the network-isolation profile was not applied (see the runbook's known limitations).
This file was transcribed from the run's captured stdout after the fact, not emitted by the test binary. Line references below are to the test file AT THE RUN'S COMMIT, not to HEAD.
